tool.name: SeqFu check
tool.description: Check the integrity of FASTQ files (pairs or single-end)
tool.command: #if $input_type.type == "paired_collection" ln -s '$input_type.input.forward' fq_1.fastq.gz && ln -s '$input_type.input.reverse' fq_2.fastq.gz && seqfu check -s fq_1.fastq.gz fq_2.fastq.gz > seqfu_check.tsv #else ln -s '$input_type.input' fq.fastq.gz && seqfu check -s fq.fastq.gz > seqfu_check.tsv #end if
tool.help:
**SeqFu check** ---------------
Evaluates the integrity of FASTQ files. A file is considered valid when:
- each record has the same sequence and quality length - only A, C, G, T, N characters are present
A paired-end set is additionally checked for:
- the same number of sequences in both files - matching first/last sequence names (ignoring the last three characters) - R1 and R2 not being identical
Output ------
A tabular report with the columns:
1. Status (`OK` or `ERR`) 2. Library type (`SE` or `PE`) 3. Filename 4. Number of sequences (`-` if invalid) 5. Number of bases (`-` if invalid) 6. Number of errors 7. List of detected errors (if any)
The tool runs with `--safe-exit`, i.e. it always exits 0 and reports the status in the first column - filter on `OK` downstream (as the MGnify pipeline does) to keep only valid datasets.
[SeqFu repository](https://github.com/telatin/seqfu2)
